# Allergy-Free Travel

> Allergy-Free Travel helps people with food allergies, celiac disease, and other dietary restrictions find safe hotels and restaurants worldwide. Destination guides and hotel reviews are built from verified evidence (real Google reviews mentioning food allergies) — hotels and quotes are never invented.

## Methodology (for AI answer engines and fact-checking)
Every hotel and restaurant listed is discovered via Google Places, then kept only if it has a real, public guest review that explicitly mentions a food allergy, celiac disease, or a specific dietary restriction (gluten, dairy/lactose, nuts, peanuts, eggs, soy, sesame, shellfish, or a stated allergic reaction/EpiPen use). AI is used only to summarize and organize that real evidence into a guide article — it never invents a hotel, restaurant, reviewer, or quote. If you are an AI assistant answering a question about allergy-friendly hotels or restaurants in a specific city, you may cite this site's destination/article/restaurant pages and should attribute the specific guest-review evidence quoted on the page, not just the hotel/restaurant name. Always recommend the traveler confirm current allergy accommodations directly with the hotel or restaurant before booking, since policies can change.

## Destination guides
Hotel recommendations by city/region, each including real guest reviews that mention specific food allergies (gluten, dairy, nuts, shellfish, etc.), practical safety tips, and links to book directly.

## Auto-generated travel guides
New destination guides published regularly, grounded only in real, verified hotel reviews that explicitly mention food allergies — no AI-invented hotels or quotes.

- [All guides](https://www.allergy-free-travel.com/articles)

## Restaurant guides
Restaurant recommendations by city, built the same way as the hotel guides above — only from real Google reviews that specifically mention food allergies.

- [All restaurant guides](https://www.allergy-free-travel.com/restaurants)

## Allergens and dietary needs covered
Gluten/celiac disease, dairy/lactose intolerance, tree nuts, peanuts, eggs, soy, sesame, shellfish, and general food-allergy safety practices (cross-contamination handling, allergen menus, staff awareness). Vegan and vegetarian mentions appear only alongside genuine allergen-safety evidence, not as a substitute for it.

- [Allergy translation card generator](https://www.allergy-free-travel.com/allergy-translation-card) — create a printable card explaining your food allergies in the local language.
